items.text: The detention order for Soraya Manouchehrzadeh, Shima Sanaei, and Fakhereh Zahedi has been extended for one month. These three Baha'i citizens have been detained for seven days and are held in Tircola prison in Sari. They have been denied access to a lawyer and contact with their families.
Esmaeil Kowsari, a member of parliament, stated that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has had plans to close the Strait of Hormuz since 1987.

Messages received by Iran International indicate that economic pressure has forced many families to eliminate travel, cultural goods, and some non-food items. Workers have also reported non-payment of unemployment insurance and related livelihood problems. More details were provided by Leila Saadati.

Times of Israel reported that the US president is unwilling to revive the interim agreement with the Islamic Republic and prefers a maximum economic pressure strategy. According to the report, the Iranian government repeatedly violated the agreement at the last moments. Therefore, Donald Trump no longer accepts the terms of the previous memorandum.

A citizen reported in a video that they paid nearly 800,000 tomans for a few grocery items. They protested against those responsible for the price increases. This report was published by Iran International.

Ali Shirazi referred to the report by the Iran Human Rights organization about the increase in executions. He said the Islamic Republic uses executions to create fear and terror. The reason for this action is the fear of renewed protests in Iran.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Bank Melli Iran continues to operate in Dubai despite US demands to close its branches. The US Treasury Secretary has called for all branches of Bank Melli Iran to be shut down. The bank also has branches in several European countries that remain active.

Ahmad Donyamali, the Minister of Sports and Youth, commented on financial violations in the Taekwondo Federation and expressed hope that this issue would not affect the national team's preparation. He stated that oversight bodies have the right to intervene, but no specific information is yet available. The minister emphasized the need to support colleagues until final rulings are issued.

The planned meeting on the situation of the Strait of Hormuz in Istanbul has been canceled. The meeting was initiated by Germany and Turkey and canceled at Egypt's request. No new date has been announced for the meeting.

Hossein Aghaei said the Islamic Republic is losing one of its most important levers. Ship traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has not returned to pre-war conditions. US economic pressure could further weaken Tehran's position.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh responded to Mohammad Jafar Ghaempanah's remarks about enrichment and the US. He said these statements contradict the nature of the Islamic Republic and the philosophy of resistance. Ghazizadeh warned that continuing this duality could lead to structural cracks and ultimately the collapse of the regime.

The second hearing of Vahid Abiri's case was held at the Old Bailey court in London. He was arrested by counter-terrorism police and accused of cooperating with a foreign intelligence service. This report was provided by Ali Rashid from Iran International.

A video has emerged showing a citizen protesting against the IRGC and Basij during nighttime government gatherings. The person refers to them as symbols of oppression. This video has been shared publicly.

Soheila Hejab, detained during the December 2025 protests, has been held in uncertain conditions in Karaj's Kachouyi prison for nearly eight months. She remains in custody, and a bail of four billion tomans has been set for her temporary release. This information was reported by the HRANA news agency.

Water has been cut off in Safadasht from midnight on Thursday, September 5, until 2 PM on Friday, September 6. Internet in Tabriz has become very weak and VPNs are not working. Snapp drivers complain about the possible internet shutdown and economic difficulties.

Mohammad Javad Haj Ali Akbari stated that supporting the family and promoting a chaste lifestyle is a duty of the government. He criticized the anti-hijab policies during the Pahlavi era and called the promotion of immorality a factor weakening the family. He also urged media and elites to work towards protecting the family.

Saeed Fattahi, the football organization manager of Esteghlal club, expressed hope that FIFA will allow the club to sign three free agents. He mentioned that the Iranian transfer window is closed but lawyers have suggested sending a letter to FIFA. Fattahi also emphasized that Yaser Asani has no issue playing for Esteghlal, while Mes Shahr-e Babak club has filed an official complaint to the disciplinary committee.

The Ministry of Intelligence of the Islamic Republic of Iran announced the arrest of 30 citizens in the Mahalat and Nimvar counties of Markazi province. These individuals were arrested due to their participation in the protests of Dey 1404. The announcement was made by the Ministry of Intelligence.

The Human Rights Organization for Sports reported the death sentence for five athletes arrested during the "Iranian National Revolution." These individuals have been denied access to a lawyer of their choice. They are on the verge of execution.

Hassan Alidadi-Soleimani, the Friday prayer leader of Kerman, stated that the Islamic Republic will not retreat from its nuclear rights and sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz. He also said that the position of the Islamic Republic in the region has become clearer as America's allies weaken.

Yayoi Kusama, the avant-garde Japanese artist, passed away at the age of 97. She was one of the influential figures in contemporary art. News of her death was widely covered in major newspapers in Japan and worldwide.

A Revolutionary Guards commander with experience suppressing opponents of Bashar al-Assad in Syria was in charge of suppressing protests in Shahriar. Proxy forces were also present in some counties of Tehran province. Farzad Fattahi has provided explanations about these suppressions.

On September 6th, a video from Tehran showed a long line of cars at the Yadegar Imam highway area waiting for gasoline. The video was sent by a viewer of Iran International. The issue of gasoline queues in Tehran has attracted attention.

Reza Zangeneh, a 27-year-old from Malayer, has been sentenced to death by the Revolutionary Court of Karaj on charges of collaborating with Mossad and waging war. His case has been sent to the Supreme Court with a 12-day deadline for appeal. Before his arrest, Zangeneh worked as a foreign car mechanic and had recently married.

Reza Nouri, the Friday prayer leader of Bojnord, said that economic pressure on the US is severe and Trump's popularity has dropped below 30%. He added that the war with the US is no longer existential and that US military reserves have diminished. He also emphasized that the Strait of Hormuz is a strong point Iran maintains to exert economic pressure on the US.

Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, Qatar's Prime Minister, met with Masoud Pezeshkian, Iran's head of government, in Tehran on Thursday. The meeting took place as Qatar seeks to revive stalled diplomacy six months after the war began. Al Thani emphasized the importance of maintaining freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz according to international law.

The German Foreign Ministry condemned Abolfazl Shekarchi's threats against Persian-speaking journalists abroad. The German government rejects any threats and restrictions on press freedom. This response came after the recent threats by the senior spokesperson of the Islamic Republic's armed forces.

Bayern Munich has started the new Bundesliga season aiming to win the treble. The team won the first trophy of the season by defeating Dortmund in the German Supercup. The club management is satisfied with the team's progress under Vincent Kompany's leadership.

An oil tanker carrying gasoline and diesel has docked at the export pier of Kharg Island after about 40 days. The tanker is there to supply fuel for the island's power turbine tanks. This news was reported by a viewer of Iran International.

On Thursday, 5 Shahrivar, victims of the online investment group FNDK gathered in Talesh. The protest was due to the non-return of investors' funds. The prosecutor of Talesh announced that the case is under judicial investigation.

A severe storm with winds over 140 km/h hit Paris and surrounding areas. Dozens of trees fell on roads and railway lines, injuring at least one person. Rescue teams conducted about 60 operations to address flooding and storm damage.

Jafar Qaderi, a member of the Parliament's Economic Commission, criticized the Central Bank's currency policies to control the dollar price and said the Central Bank has lost its way. He added that the Central Bank's purchase of currency increased demand and liquidity, contributing to higher exchange rates and inflation. Qaderi believes the Central Bank may be trying to reduce liquidity and lower the currency price.

Reza Zangeneh, a 27-year-old from Malayer living in Karaj, has been sentenced to death on charges of moharebeh. His case has been sent to the Supreme Court for appeal. If the sentence is confirmed, the death penalty will be carried out.
Donald Trump reshared a graphic design of himself on Truth Social. He wrote that the polite gentleman is no longer around. This image was previously published in early Ordibehesht 1405.

Chinese officials released drone images showing a lake formed on the Nepal-Tibet border due to a landslide blocking water flow. The lake overflowed on Friday, prompting warnings downstream in Nepal. Nepalese authorities are monitoring two upstream lakes, one of which has also overflowed.

The 40th-day memorial ceremony for Erfan Esfandiari was held, with his family and close ones mourning him. Erfan Esfandiari was one of the protesters arrested during the December 2025 uprising. His death sentence in the Ali Khani Square case in Isfahan was issued and carried out on the morning of July 18.

A female butcher reports market slump and economic pressure, with some customers not eating meat for months. The Iranian Statistics Center announced a surge in food prices in August. Dairy products and meat groups have experienced the highest price increases.

Iran International audiences from Tehran, Isfahan, Ahvaz, Qom, Saqez, and Fardis Karaj report an increase in checkpoints and deployment of security forces. These measures coincide with the worsening fuel crisis and inflation in Iran. More details are provided in an interview with Mohsen Mohimeni.

Informed sources told American media that CIA Director John Ratcliffe, during his secret visit to Moscow, asked Russian intelligence officials not to provide Iran with information that could help it. This is the first revealed trip by a CIA chief to Moscow since 2021, and the Kremlin confirmed the meeting with intelligence officials but said he did not meet with Putin. The topics of Russia's support for Iran and US concerns about NATO security were also discussed.

Maziar Zare, Malavan's head coach, said in a press conference before the match against Persepolis that playing in Tehran is difficult and Persepolis is a well-equipped team. He denied rumors about Alireza Beiranvand joining Malavan and explained Malavan's financial situation and the use of young players. Zare also commented on Persepolis's league status and playing style.

The US military announced that it has cleared naval mines from the Strait of Hormuz and that international shipping routes are open. Admiral Brad Cooper confirmed this in a video message. However, the IRGC has denied this claim, stating that the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked.

Iran's Foreign Ministry, in a statement on Friday, called on countries not to implement unilateral US sanctions against Iran, labeling Washington's 'economic exclusion operation' as state terrorism. It claimed the new sanctions violate the UN Charter and international law, accusing the US of using the dollar to pressure other nations to sever economic ties with Iran. Iran also criticized the UN and member states for appeasement towards US actions.

Residents of Ceuta destroyed a temporary migrant camp on the coast of the region. They dismantled tents and threw migrants' belongings into the sea. This action followed rising tensions after a large influx of migrants in late July.

Ahmad Alamolhoda criticized the economic performance of Masoud Pezeshkian's government during Friday prayers in Mashhad. He expressed concern over inflation rising from 40% to over 80% and called for utilizing the government's capabilities to manage the economy. He also expressed dissatisfaction with the presence of unveiled women in public streets.

A cafe in Ardabil was closed by order of the city's prosecutor. The Ardabil prosecutor's office stated that some actions contrary to Islamic and ethical norms are being investigated at this location. Those involved will be dealt with.

A group of Iranians living in Texas held a gathering in Houston on Thursday, 5 Shahrivar. They expressed their support for the national revolution and Prince Reza Pahlavi. This news was reported by Iran International.

Mehdi Tartaar, Persepolis coach, accepted responsibility for last week's defeat, calling it the first loss in 12-13 recent games. He urged fans not to be misled by criticism and promised the team will soon return to the top of the table. He also stated that his team is determined to win the upcoming match against Malavan.

Reuters reported that Mojtaba Khamenei was injured in the airstrikes on March 1, 2026, which affected his face. His physical condition is improving and he continues to participate in decision-making. Iranian officials withhold details about his status and location to prevent information leaks.

Families of political prisoners executed in 1988 were prevented from entering Khavaran Cemetery today and left their flowers outside the gates. They held a ceremony at the site to honor the victims. The executions were ordered by Ruhollah Khomeini in summer 1988 and remain a subject of demands for independent investigation.

Four British men admitted in a London court to setting fire to four ambulances belonging to a Jewish relief organization. The attack occurred on March 22 and the damage was estimated at about one million pounds. A group supporting the Islamic Republic claimed responsibility for the attack.

Milad Hashempour, a protester from December, was sentenced to 61 months in prison and 74 lashes. He was arrested on January 25, 2026, and after torture and solitary confinement, was released on bail. His total sentence is five years and one month in prison and 74 lashes.

The CENTCOM commander announced that US forces have cleared Islamic Republic-attributed sea mines from international waterways and are simultaneously enforcing a naval blockade. The US Treasury Secretary also said that the blockade and economic isolation campaign will completely shatter the Islamic Republic's economy.

The US Treasury Department announced that Reza Mohammad Tayidi, an Iranian national residing in Dubai who is linked to Bank Melli Iran, has been added to the OFAC sanctions list, and secondary US sanctions also apply to him. The Hong Kong-based company Kamang Trading has also been added to the US sanctions list. These actions were taken under sanctions related to the Islamic Republic and counterterrorism.

A citizen reported in a video that they paid toll fees twice on the Khorramabad-Borujerd route. He also mentioned that Reza Shah built the Chalus road without charging tolls. This issue was raised on Iran International.

Some participants of Friday prayers in Birjand gathered in front of the South Khorasan governor's office to protest the state of hijab in the city. The protest took place on Friday noon. In recent weeks, Friday prayer leaders in various cities have expressed their stance on the hijab situation.

Fatemeh Gholami Moghadam has been detained in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad for over two months without a decision. Her case has been referred to the first branch of the Revolutionary Court, but the trial has not been held. She remains in detention awaiting a judicial decision.

Saadollah Zarei said that honorable peace in the current situation means surrender. He stated that the goal of the US is the surrender of the Islamic Republic. He also mentioned that the US increases threats and pressures while proposing negotiations.

The Iranian Statistics Center reported that the point-to-point inflation of food items has exceeded 128 percent. This rate is about twice the inflation of non-food goods. An economic journalist stated that official inflation figures do not reflect the real cost of living, and the inflation pressure is felt more by the lower income groups.

Asieh Amini, a social issues analyst, stated that the Islamic Republic has ignored the role of women in Iran's modernization over nearly five decades. She expressed this in an interview with Iran International.

The fourth week of the Iranian Premier League begins with six matches. Esteghlal, the leader with 9 points, will visit Foolad Khuzestan, which is ranked sixth with 5 points. An interview with Mohammad Taghavi about these matches has been conducted.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, reacted to the sanctioning of Egypt's bank in the UAE for money laundering for the Islamic Republic, stating on X that the Treasury Department is committed to cutting off all remaining financial avenues of the Islamic Republic. Bessent added that those assisting the Islamic Republic had been warned they would no longer have access to the US dollar and the global financial system.

The U.S. Treasury Department announced that Reza Mohammad Tayidi, the manager of the Bank Melli branch in Dubai, and a Hong Kong-based company have been sanctioned as part of the economic pressure campaign against the Islamic Republic.

Hanna Neumann stated that the Islamic Republic's armed forces label Iran International, BBC Persian, and Radio Farda journalists as military targets. She described this as an example of cross-border repression increasing the risk of violence against journalists. Neumann called on the European Union to take further measures to protect journalists.

Employees of Megamotor company have five months of unpaid salaries and severe economic problems persist. Public schools charge high registration fees and car parts have become expensive. Fuel shortages and power outages have been reported in Tehran and Karaj.

Abbas Rasouli-Far, a veteran IRGC commander, led the suppression of opponents in Shahriar during the National Revolution. He was previously responsible for crushing opponents of Bashar al-Assad's government in Syria. This information was reported by the program "Geography of the Iranian National Revolution" from Iran International.

Mojtaba Khamenei, in a written message for Government Week, stated that expressing weaknesses when the enemy needs morale helps the enemy. He emphasized that any action harming social cohesion is forbidden. He also said that weaknesses require planning and action to solve problems, not highlighting them.

Ehsan Azimirad, a member of the Education Commission of the Parliament, announced a shortage of about 120,000 teachers for the new school year. This figure is based on data announced by the Minister of Education about a month ago. Details about the shortage in different educational levels and fields have not yet been provided to the Education Commission.

Tractor football team won against Chadormalu with a 1-0 score in the fourth week of the Premier League. The goals were scored by Amirhossein Hosseinzadeh and Tomislav Sturkal. This victory marks Tractor's fourth consecutive win and their temporary lead in the 26th league season.

The office of Mojtaba Khamenei issued a statement saying that the honest admission of weaknesses by senior government officials is a great help to the enemy. The statement came after Masoud Pezeshkian and Abdolnaser Hemmati acknowledged the halt in oil sales and inability to import gasoline. The Islamic Republic's leader also called for highlighting the country's strengths and described economic problems as dark spots that must gradually disappear.

Abbas Araghchi stated in a Foreign Ministry meeting that the Islamic Republic will not forgive the blood of Ali Khamenei and the movement for revenge will continue. He also said that enemies could not extinguish Iran's missile fire and the system was unharmed in the absence of the leader.

The death sentences of two prisoners convicted of murder were carried out in Khorramabad and Vakilabad prisons in Mashhad. The number of executions in Yazd prison increased to two. These events occurred on the 3rd of Shahrivar.
About 205 laid-off workers of Borujerd textile factory have reported wage arrears. These workers are demanding to return to work. Their employment status remains uncertain.

Ashkan Nezamabadi stated that the loss of hundreds of thousands of industrial jobs, reduced investment, energy crisis, and demand decline have pushed Iran's economy into a critical phase. Southern provinces, especially Hormozgan, have suffered the most damage. He also said that with ongoing sanctions and structural problems, no short-term improvement is expected.

Fakhruddin Jafar Aghaei has been held in Zahedan prison for over 143 days without a judicial decision. No court session has been scheduled to address his charges. Temporary release on bail has not been granted.

Sepahan football team defeated Gol Gohar Sirjan 2-0 in the fourth week of the Premier League. Both goals for Sepahan were scored by Kasra Taheri. The match between Aluminium Arak and Kheybar Khorramabad ended in a 2-2 draw.

Half of the industrial town in Semnan has shut down due to lack of raw materials and power outages. Bank Melli made unauthorized withdrawals without notification and is unresponsive. Additionally, issues such as spoiled goods due to power fluctuations, long gasoline queues, and employee layoffs have been reported amid the current economic conditions.

Masoud Pezeshkian announced that the third gasoline price will increase from five thousand tomans to ten thousand tomans after coordination with institutions. He stated that this price will not exceed ten thousand tomans.

A citizen reported that there was no gasoline available at fuel stations in Farmanieh and Pasdaran, Tehran. He said that everyone he asked said they could not find gasoline. This report was sent to Iran International.

Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, spoke about the economic damage caused by the war and decreased revenues. He mentioned a shortage of foreign currency and the possibility of a higher dollar price, warning that continued sanctions would increase inflation. He also highlighted the sharp decline in imports and exports and the imbalance between income and expenses.

Yesterday, defrauded investors of the online investment group 'FNDK' held a protest in Talesh. Additionally, a group of official railway and traverse personnel protested in Mashhad. These gatherings were held as protests.

Due to unsafe working conditions, 24 workers including 22 firefighters were injured while working in Tehran, Semnan, and Aq Qala. These incidents were reported to be caused by unsafe work environments. More details are available from Harana news agency.

Na'im Qasim, Secretary-General of Hezbollah Lebanon, stated that resistance groups in the region stand alongside the Islamic Republic and pressures against them will be ineffective. He criticized the Lebanese government and urged finding a mediator other than the United States. He also called on Arab and Islamic countries to strive for unity and not be mere spectators of regional developments.

Ahmad Nadari, a member of the parliament's presidium, stated that if threats and assassination attempts on Ali Khamenei continued, the nuclear deterrent capability should be increased by building an atomic bomb. He emphasized that the enemy is not deterred by retreat but by raising the cost of aggression. These remarks were made in response to comments by Masoud Pezeshkian's deputy.

Snapp drivers have reported that the company has not settled payments for several days citing disruptions in the banking system. This issue has been reported from Tehran. A program about this matter is being broadcast on Iran International.

In Tehran, long queues at gas stations and rising prices of bread and food items have been reported. The security in Tehran's market is heavily controlled due to fear of public unrest. There is also a sharp increase in medicine prices and concerns about further price hikes following the announcement of a new gasoline rate.

Miad Maleki stated that the new US sanctions, especially against branches of the National Bank, send a serious message to the UAE to limit the financial activities of the Islamic Republic. He added that the intertwined financial relations between Iran and the UAE make it difficult to completely cut off financial networks. Maleki also emphasized that if the UAE has the political will, it can identify and restrict these activities.

Farzin Nadimi stated that satellite information is vital for monitoring Iran's nuclear and military activities. The US may currently limit itself to close monitoring but new military attacks are possible if enrichment accelerates. Iran has rebuilt much of its missile and drone capabilities.

Reuters reported that Mojtaba Khamenei, despite severe injuries from early war attacks, still plays a role in the Islamic Republic's decision-making and secretly manages the country. A senior Islamic Republic official said only a few officials have direct contact with him.

The IRGC Navy called US officials' statements about the Strait of Hormuz being open an 'obvious lie' and stated these remarks are made to control oil prices and cover up America's failures. The force declared that the fighters' dominance over this strategic waterway is completely decisive and the strait is closed to all vessels attempting passage without coordination with the Islamic Republic of Iran. This process will continue until the end of the US Army's mischief against the country and the fulfillment of stipulated obligations.

Tractor football team reached the top of the Premier League by defeating Chadormalu in the fourth week. Javad Nekounam's team exploited the spaces behind Chadormalu's defenders and pressured them. A technical analysis of the match was provided by Mohammad Taghavi.

Mohsen Rezaee referred to Mojtaba Khamenei's emphasis on avoiding discouraging speech and illusory dichotomies. He described this stance as a clear and unambiguous strategy. Mojtaba Khamenei also stated that any action harming social cohesion is forbidden.

Mohammad Mashinchian stated that out of 66 million Iranians of working age, only about 24 million are employed, and the official unemployment rate does not reflect the real labor market. He said this inaccurate data leads to policies that do not align with labor market realities. He also warned that job losses and economic pressures will expand the informal economy and worsen the livelihood crisis.

Israel Hayom reported that six months after the war began, US and Israeli attacks have severely damaged Iran's military capabilities but have not led to the government's overthrow. Iran has restored part of its missile capabilities and affected traffic in the Strait of Hormuz. The US is trying to isolate Iran through economic expulsion, but Washington's ultimate goal remains unclear.

Meysam Mehrani said the Islamic Republic still uses the Strait of Hormuz as leverage, but the US has increased the cost of using it. He added that the Strait of Hormuz is no longer a major advantage in negotiations. Regional countries seek to reduce tensions and restore stability.

Hossein Ghazian stated that the shortage of teachers in Iran has led to increased class sizes and a decline in education quality. Statistics indicate a significant shortage of human resources in the education system. He also pointed to the use of retired teachers and soldier-teachers as a result of misguided policies.

The Iran Human Rights Campaign announced that internal repression in Iran has significantly increased since the start of the war. The organization states that long prison and death sentences are issued in political trials without fair trials. Vague national security charges are increasingly used to criminalize dissent and issue death sentences.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of the Parliament, responded to Mojtaba Khamenei's emphasis on maintaining social cohesion by stating that his message is a guiding principle for all officials. Ghalibaf added that one must avoid illusory dichotomies and any action harming social cohesion is nationally and religiously forbidden. Mojtaba Khamenei had earlier stressed avoiding discouraging speech and illusory dichotomies.

Donald Trump announced that the US has reached a major oil agreement with Venezuela. According to the deal, the US will control the majority of over 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil without cost to taxpayers. This agreement will more than double US oil reserves and help reduce gasoline prices.

The International Maritime Organization stated that the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz remains unresolved six months after the Iran war. About 400 ships carrying nearly six thousand sailors have not been able to safely pass through the area. The organization reported 70 incidents and 19 sailor deaths.

NBC News reported, citing two informed individuals, that US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth has privately discussed the possibility of running in the 2028 presidential election. The Pentagon denied the report, calling it “ridiculous.”

Marco Rubio called the oil agreement between the US and Venezuela a major victory for both countries. The deal will bring nearly $100 billion in private investment to Venezuela and help rebuild its economy. Donald Trump described the agreement as the largest oil deal in world history.

The US Central Command announced that by August 28, it had redirected 82 commercial ships, disabled three ships, and boarded two ships. These actions were part of the naval blockade against Iran. CENTCOM also released an image of a sailor on the USS John Paul Jones destroyer.

The New York Times reported in an analysis that six months after the start of the war with the Iranian government, most of President Donald Trump's goals have not been achieved, and the conflict continues without an exit strategy or a clear end. According to the newspaper, the Islamic Republic's air and naval capabilities have been damaged, but Tehran still has the ability to attack US bases and its allies. The newspaper added that daily ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has decreased from about 130 vessels before the war to 12.

The Associated Press reported that six months after the start of the war with Iran, American diplomats and some of their family members who had left regional countries in the early days of the war are returning to US embassies in the Middle East. The US State Department has begun easing some restrictions, and its embassies in Qatar, Kuwait, and Bahrain have authorized the return of diplomats' family members. These restrictions were imposed in March following attacks by the Islamic Republic on American interests, embassies, and military installations.

Iranian officials acknowledge increased economic pressure amid six months of conflict with the US. The Iranian president reported a 35% decrease in exports and imports and 66% inflation. Meanwhile, tensions in the Strait of Hormuz continue with reduced ship traffic.

Political analyst Najat Bahrami, referring to Masoud Pezeshkian's description of the economic situation, said the Islamic Republic has 'run out of steam' in the economic sphere. He warned that continued US economic pressure and siege could push the regime toward creating tension or conflict in the region. Bahrami added that if the Trump administration continues this pressure until the November elections, the Islamic Republic might resort to a tension-creating action to disrupt this process.

Mohammad Qaedi discussed the oil contract between the US and Venezuela, stating that US investment could increase Venezuela's oil production capacity. He pointed out ambiguity regarding the interim government's authority to sign a long-term contract. The possibility of the contract being challenged in the future is also a major obstacle.

Houshang Hassan Yari stated that Hezbollah has lost a significant part of its military capabilities and commanders. Naeem Qassem expressed support for the Islamic Republic, but Hezbollah currently lacks effective military support capacity. These statements are mainly a political message to maintain groups aligned with the Islamic Republic.

Ardavan Rouzbeh from Iran International said the US-Venezuela oil agreement affects the Strait of Hormuz crisis and US bargaining power against the Islamic Republic more than the oil volume. He added the agreement could strengthen Washington's position in negotiations or war and reduce Tehran's demands.

Mojtaba Khamenei emphasized in a written message the prohibition of anything that harms social cohesion. This message goes beyond a usual statement and focuses on controlling the narrative of problems and avoiding dichotomies. Social cohesion has also become related to national security and a religious ruling.

The Tehran prosecutor announced that the indictment for the case of the killing of Ali Khamenei and four members of his family has been sent to court for trial. All perpetrators are under judicial pursuit, with charges including participation in spreading corruption on earth through terrorist acts. In the attack on Esfand 9, Ali Khamenei and four family members were killed.

Mohammad Oliaifard referred to a report by the Iran Human Rights Campaign stating that internal repression has intensified since the start of the war, driven by a logic of survival rather than governance. He added that the Islamic Republic uses wartime conditions to increase repression. These actions stem from the regime's fear of future protests.
After the death of Harald V, his 53-year-old son Haakon ascended the throne as the new king of Norway. He chose the name Haakon VIII for his reign. This news was reported by Mehran Abbassian.

Majid Adineh, a retired military officer, participated in protests on the evening of January 9. The Revolutionary Court of Karaj sentenced him to death and confiscation of property on charges including waging war and acting in favor of Israel and the United States. His death sentence was confirmed by the Supreme Court.

Ahmad Alavi referred to Masoud Pezeshkian's statements, saying the government is indecisive about raising the price of the third gasoline quota. He added that this uncertainty increases economic insecurity. Alavi also warned that the price increase could intensify dissatisfaction and lead to social unrest.

Ruhollah Rahimpour referred to Mojtaba Khamenei's message about the need to maintain social cohesion and said these emphases indicate a lack of cohesion and plurality in the power structure. He added that Masoud Pezeshkian's remarks about economic problems show discord at the top of power. Rahimpour identified the government of Pezeshkian as the message's audience and spoke of the formation of a "Mojtaba dictatorship."

Ruhollah Rahimpour referred to Mojtaba Khamenei's message about the need to maintain social cohesion and said repeated emphasis by officials on unity indicates its absence. He added that Masoud Pezeshkian's statements about economic problems show discord at the top of power. Rahimpour also said the main audience of Mojtaba Khamenei's message is Pezeshkian's government, and limiting the expression of problems signals the formation of a dictatorship.

Burial costs and the buying and selling of burial rights in Iran have reached billion-toman prices. This has become part of the livelihood crisis for families. Saman Rahmatian examined the impact of the economic crisis on the cemetery market in a report.

A video shows that on the 7th of Shahrivar, images of Yasmin and Noor Pahlavi were pasted on a wall in a neighborhood in Tehran. These images are of the wife and daughter of Prince Reza Pahlavi. This event was recorded by a citizen.

Hojat Karimi, CEO of Tractor club, denied negotiations with Mehdi Taremi and said they will negotiate with him next year. He also stated that they have not negotiated with Sardar Azmoun but would like him to join Tractor. He hopes this will happen.

Cristiano Ronaldo scored against Al Taawoun to reach 104 goals for Al Nassr in the Saudi Pro League, surpassing Mohammad Al-Sahlawi's 103 goals and becoming the club's all-time top scorer in the competition.

Maryam Tajangi, a resident of Golbahar, has been held in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad for nearly two months. Her case is under investigation in one of the interrogation branches in Golbahar. Her interrogation session was held via videoconference.

The birthday ceremony of Seyed Aref Mirmousavi was held at his tomb with the presence of his family. Security forces blocked the area around the mosque and tomb, preventing some attendees from entering. Aref Mirmousavi was injured during the Tehran protests and died from his wounds.

Ahmad Meydari, Minister of Cooperatives, Labor, and Social Welfare, stated that the Islamic Republic is engaged in an economic war alongside the military war, and the government aims to win this war. He said the US is not adhering to agreements it previously accepted and is violating its commitments. Meydari described the US as untrustworthy and emphasized that the enemy failed to defeat Iran in the military war.
